newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND BEAT PAKISTAN, BUT LOSE SERIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND BEAT PAKISTAN, BUT LOSE SERIES.

text.p: New Zealand ended their four-week tour of Pakistan on a winning note when they outplayed their hosts to take a seven-wicket victory in the final one-day international of the three-match series on Sunday.

Chasing Pakistan's 234 for four in 50 overs on an easy-paced wicket, New Zealand overhauled the home team's score with 4.5 overs to spare to register their first one-day win in Pakistan since 1984. But they still lost the series 2-1.
New Zealand's cause was eased by openers Brian Young (32) and man-of-the-match Nathan Astle (60), who put on 96 for the first wicket in 101 balls.
Though both departed in the space of 10 balls, Adam Parore and Stephen Fleming kept up the pace, sharing an 84-run third-wicket partnership that lasted 102 balls.
When Parore fell with the score at 183 after contributing 47, Fleming and Chris Cairns steered New Zealand to victory without any further damage.
Fleming remained unbeaten on 48 from 60 balls with six boundaries while Cairns contributed a very fine 26, spiced with a six and a four.
Astle, promoted in the batting order, made Pakistan's bowling look very mediocre in the absence of Waqar Younis. He slammed six boundaries and a six in his 60 off 68 balls.
Earlier, Pakistan, making first use of the wicket after winning the toss, managed to reach 234 for four in 50 overs.

The respectable total was largely due to a swashbuckling 39-ball 66 by skipper Wasim Akram who shared a face-saving 108-run partnership with Ijaz Ahmad in 75 balls after Pakistan were only on 126 for four after 37.5 overs.
Wasim blasted five sixes and four boundaries while Ijaz scored an unbeaten 73 from 87 balls with the aid of six fours.

Wasim severely punished Justin Vaughan, hitting him for 21 runs in his final over, including two sixes and two fours. That spoiled Vaughan's figures who finished with one for 59 after conceding 14 runs from his opening six-over spell.
Zahoor Elahi was the other main run-getter for Pakistan, scoring 51 runs from 99 balls with the help of six boundaries and a six over point off Cairns.
The two-match test series, which ended a week ago, was tied 1-1.
